title: Which pot made it spicy?
allegory: Direct feature attribution is tracing a flavour in a bowl back to its pots: the cook ladled from pots along the counter (attention), a taster scores the bowl for one flavour (the latent), and because tasting is fair, the score splits exactly into each ladle's size times its pot's flavour.
map: source positions, each with its value vector
how big a ladle comes from each pot
the attention weight from the destination to that source
the attention output at the destination: a weighted sum of values
a taster scoring one flavour, before rounding down to 'none'
the SAE latent's encoder direction, a linear score before the ReLU
each pot's share of the flavour
DFA: attention weight × (value · encoder direction) for that source

chapters.name: Where from, exactly?
chapters.note: which earlier word woke this feature?

cap.1: A feature detector lights up on one word. But attention blended in bits of many earlier words to get there. Which earlier word is the reason?
cap.2: An SAE latent trained on an attention layer's output fires at a destination token. That output mixes many source positions. DFA asks which sources caused the activation.
cap.3: For an SAE on attention output, the latent's activation at destination d depends on values from every source s the heads attended to. DFA decomposes it by source position.

cap.1: Picture a cook filling one bowl with ladles from pots along the counter: a big ladle from some, a drop from others. A taster scores the bowl for one flavour.
cap.2: Attention output at a position = sum over sources of (attention weight × value). The SAE latent scores that output with its encoder direction, like a taster scoring one flavour.
cap.3: z_d = Σ_s A[d, s] v_s per head. The latent's pre-activation is w_enc · (z_d − b_dec) + b_enc, which is linear in z_d.

cap.1: Tasting is fair: the bowl's score is exactly each ladle's size times its pot's flavour, added up. So you can read off each pot's share. That is DFA.
cap.2: The latent's pre-activation is linear in the attention output, and that output is a weighted sum of values, so the score splits into one term per source position, and per head.
cap.3: DFA_s = Σ_h A_h[d, s] (v_{s,h} · w_enc,h) for fixed patterns; the terms sum exactly to the pre-activation minus the bias constant. The exercise is deriving this.

chapters.name: Each pot's share
chapters.title: toy DFA: share = ladle × flavour; the shares sum to 1.25

cap.1: Four pots. Share = ladle × flavour. Pot 1 gives a big ladle of strong flavour: 0.6 × 2 = 1.2 of the 1.25 total. Pot 2 even pulls the score down.
cap.2: DFA shares add up exactly to the latent's pre-activation, minus biases. Here source 1 supplies 1.2 of 1.25; source 2 is negative: attention that works against the latent.
cap.3: Signed, additive attributions: like DLA's negative heads, a source can oppose the latent. Check your derivation by asserting the shares sum to the pre-activation minus the bias terms.

chapters.name: Before the ReLU
chapters.verdict: Split the linear score; the ReLU is not fair.

cap.1: The taster's final verdict stops at zero: 'not spicy' covers everything from mild to minus. Split the raw score, before that cut, or the shares won't add up.
cap.2: Attribute the latent's pre-activation, not its post-ReLU value. The ReLU isn't linear, so shares of the clipped value don't sum. The bias terms belong to no source.
cap.3: Linearity holds for w_enc · (z − b_dec) + b_enc only, and its constant part is unattributable. Like DLA, DFA is direct: it credits the source read, not how that value was built.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Which earlier word woke this feature?
DLA's trick, pointed at a feature
Direct only: pair it with patching

cap.1: Knowing which earlier words switched a feature on tells you what the model was paying attention to, which is what you need before you try to steer it.
cap.2: DFA reuses DLA's trick (a linear score of a sum splits into parts) with a latent's encoder direction in place of the logit direction. Reach for patching when you need causes beyond the direct path.
cap.3: Signed, additive latent-to-source attributions make SAE features on attention layers legible; paired with causal checks they support circuit-level understanding and targeted steering.

coda.title: Move the attention between three sources and watch each source's share of the latent

caption.1: Give source A more attention and the latent lights up. Pile attention onto B and it switches off, because B's flavour works against it. Watch the shares move.
caption.2: Each bar is attention weight × (value · encoder direction). The bars plus the bias give the pre-activation exactly; the ReLU readout shows what the latent actually outputs.
caption.3: DFA_s = A[d,s](v_s · w_enc). Moving attention redistributes shares; a negative-flavour source can push the pre-activation below 0, where the ReLU hides every share.

where_else: Direct logit attribution: the same split, with the logit direction instead of a latent's
Attention analysis: weighting sources by what was read, not only where the head looked
SAE feature dashboards: finding which earlier tokens drive a latent
Accounting: splitting a total into each contributor's share, like a bill or a portfolio's return

hamming.what: Splitting an SAE latent's activation on an attention output into one signed share per source position (and head) that attention read from.
hamming.when: When a feature fires on an attention layer's output and you want to know which earlier tokens switched it on.
hamming.why: Attention hides where information came from; because the latent's score is linear before the ReLU, DFA recovers each source's share exactly.

object.title: The ladle rack
object.subtitle: One cup per (earlier word, head); each cup is as tall as the share of the feature's score that it poured in.

knobs.label: How focused the heads' attention is

cap.1: A rack of cups, one per earlier word and head. Each cup's height is how much of the feature's score it poured in.
cap.2: Bar (s, h) = head h's attention to source s × (value · encoder direction). All bars sum to the latent's pre-activation, minus biases.
cap.3: The attention-DFA tensor over (source, head); its entries sum to w_enc · z_d minus the bias constant.

cap.1: With attention spread evenly, every cup gets a little, and the shares simply follow each pot's flavour.
cap.2: Uniform attention: shares follow v · w_enc, so well-aligned values stand out a little, but nothing dominates.
cap.3: With A ≈ 1/n, DFA reduces to each source's projected value divided evenly: a flat, flavour-shaped profile.

cap.1: Sharpen the heads' focus and one cup towers: head 1 reading word 4 poured most of the score.
cap.2: Peaked attention concentrates the attribution: here head 1's read of source 4 supplies most of the pre-activation.
cap.3: DFA factorises into pattern × projected value; confident patterns localise the attribution to a few (source, head) pairs.

cap.1: From above you can read the answer straight off: which earlier word, through which head, woke this feature.
cap.2: Sum over heads for a per-source attribution; sum over sources for a per-head one.
cap.3: Both marginals of the DFA tensor are direct-path attributions; how source 4's value was built needs a separate, causal analysis.

predict.q: Why attribute the latent's pre-activation rather than its value after the ReLU?

options.t: The pre-activation is linear, so the shares add up exactly
The post-ReLU value is usually bigger

predict.why: Before the ReLU the score is a linear function of the attention output, a weighted sum over sources. The ReLU breaks that.

predict.q: A source's share comes out negative. What does that mean?

options.t: Attending to it pushed the latent down
A bug: shares must be positive

predict.why: Shares are signed: attention weight × (value · encoder direction). A value pointing against the latent's direction lowers its score.

predict.q: DFA says source 4 supplied most of the score. Does that prove source 4's word caused the feature?

options.t: No: DFA is direct only; earlier layers built that value
Yes: DFA is a full causal account

predict.why: Like DLA, DFA credits the position whose value was read. How that value got there needs patching or a further decomposition.

object.where: Any total that is a weighted sum you can split: DLA on logits, a shared bill, a portfolio's return by holding.
